<context query="Gemini agent pods MCP tools not available before 2026-09-23" template="default" budget="8000">
<section name="Architecture Decisions" source="adrs" priority="2">
<document source="adrs/ADR-031-agent-station-crds.md" type="adr" relevance="1.00" tokens="358">
## Amendment (2026-08): agents consume `resources.mcp_servers`

The recipe's `resources.mcp_servers` (defined in [ADR-030](./ADR-030-agent-definition-recipe-and-tool-seam.md))
was modeled but never injected. It is now realized end-to-end so an agent pod gets **live** Lore tools
for the run's duration, not only the one-shot pre-run context hydration:

- **Controller wiring.** The ai-agent-subsystem controller renders each `resources.mcp_servers[]` entry
  into a `.mcp.json` and passes `--mcp-config` (with `--strict-mcp-config`, since the pod cwd is `/`
  and auto-load won't fire) on the headless `claude` command; `headers_secret` resolves to the entry's
  `Authorization: Bearer` header. `disallowed_tools`/`allowed_tools` flow into
  `--disallowedTools`/`--allowedTools`.
- **Egress + gateway resolution.** The `agent-job-egress` NetworkPolicy allows egress only to public
  `:443` (DNS excepted), so in-cluster ClusterIPs are unreachable from a pod. The tools are therefore
  served by a shared **`lore-mcp` gateway** (`apps/mcp-server` in HTTP/agent mode) exposed at a public
  `:443` host — the same shape the already-shipped `output.sinks[].http` + `headers_secret` uses to
  reach a public endpoint under this policy. No NetworkPolicy change is needed. The gateway itself is a
  normal Deployment (not under `agent-job-egress`), so gateway→lore-api uses the in-cluster ClusterIP
  while agent→gateway is public `:443`.
</document>
</section>
<section name="Agent Memory" source="memories" priority="2">
<document source="session-summary/2026-09-23-gemini-mcp-v0.11.3-proven" type="memory" tokens="338">
**session-summary/2026-09-23-gemini-mcp-v0.11.3-proven** (memory): Gemini agent pods now reach the Lore MCP (proven 2026-09-23 ~21:20 UTC). Chain: subsystem #246 (init merges mcpServers into gemini-cli USER settings /agent/.gemini/settings.json via `ai-agent-init mcp-settings <file> <servers>`; the v0.11.2 system-scope file was refused for a uid-1000 dir), #247 changelog cut, tag v0.11.3, #249 agent-contracts bump 0.11.3 + manual publish-contracts dispatch, lore #2144 chart pins (controller sha256:77307751…, agent sha256:56ce7fa5…), deploy-ai-agents green 21:15 UTC. Proof: code-review run f0e87e9e (lore #2145) made mcp_lore_lore_assemble_context x1, mcp_lore_lore_search_memory x2, mcp_lore_lore_get_ci_failures x1.

Traps learned: (1) a subsystem release cut PR must ALSO bump packages/agent-contracts/package.json + lock, or the tag's publish-contracts job fails at its version guard; recovery = bump PR + `gh workflow run publish-contracts.yml --ref main` (dispatch skips the tag guard). (2) `JSONValue.emptyObject` is missing in the CI phobos (ldc); use parseJSON("{}"). (3) The run page init line reads ev.tools which Gemini's init event lacks, so it says "(0 tools)" even when MCP works — lore #2146; judge MCP health by tool_call rows. (4) Local kubectl context defaults to minikube; GKE is gke_re5-n8n-platform_europe-west1_n8n-cluster.
</document>
<document source="session:re-cinq/lore#2731" type="episode" tokens="52">
**session:re-cinq/lore#2731** (episode) [observed]: The floor chart pinned ai-agent-subsystem v0.11.10, but v0.11.11 was released on 2026-10-12 19:26 UTC with gemini-cli 0.62.0, creating a version mismatch.
</document>
<document source="session:re-cinq/ai-agent-subsystem" type="episode" tokens="44">
**session:re-cinq/ai-agent-subsystem** (episode) [observed]: Gemini agent initialization now fails immediately if downloading or unpacking the pinned gemini-cli tarball fails.
</document>
</section>
